title: Web security with a transparent proxy
blurb: Redirect web traffic to the Secure Web Appliance with WCCP and filter it by category and reputation.
scenario: Users on **10.1.1.0/24** browse through R1. Send their HTTP traffic to the **Secure Web Appliance** (formerly WSA) without touching browser settings, using **WCCP** on the LAN interface **GigabitEthernet0/1**. Then set the web reputation and URL category policy on the appliance.
topology:
Users 10.1.1.0/24 ── Gi0/1 R1 ── Internet
                       │ WCCP
                Secure Web Appliance
objectives: Compare explicit and transparent proxy deployments
Select the traffic to redirect and turn on WCCP
Set web reputation thresholds and URL categories

steps.title: Explicit or transparent?
steps.learn: An **explicit** proxy is set in the browser or through a PAC/WPAD file, and the client knows it's talking to a proxy. A **transparent** proxy receives traffic redirected by the network (WCCP or policy-based routing), and the client doesn't know.
steps.question: Why use a transparent deployment with WCCP here?

options.text: Every device that browses through R1 is covered without changing browser or OS settings, and WCCP can bypass the proxy if it fails.
Transparent mode is the only way to filter HTTPS.
options.why: Both modes can inspect HTTPS with decryption. The difference is how the traffic reaches the proxy.

options.text: Transparent mode needs no network changes.
options.why: It does: the router or switch must redirect traffic with WCCP or PBR.

steps.title: Turn on WCCP redirection
steps.learn: The **web-cache** service (service 0) redirects TCP port 80. A **redirect list** limits which traffic is sent to the proxy, and `ip wccp web-cache redirect in` on the LAN interface intercepts it as it enters R1.
steps.task: Create ACL **WCCP-REDIRECT** that permits TCP from **10.1.1.0/24** to any on **www**. Turn on the **web-cache** service with that redirect list, and redirect **inbound** on **GigabitEthernet0/1**.
steps.hint: `ip access-list extended WCCP-REDIRECT`, `permit tcp 10.1.1.0 0.0.0.255 any eq www`, `ip wccp web-cache redirect-list WCCP-REDIRECT`, `interface GigabitEthernet0/1`, `ip wccp web-cache redirect in`.

steps.title: Web reputation thresholds
steps.learn: **Web Based Reputation Scores** (WBRS) run from −10 to +10. The default access policy blocks the worst sites, scans the middle with the anti-malware engines, and allows the best without scanning.
steps.screen: Secure Web Appliance › Web Security Manager › Access Policies › Web Reputation and Anti-Malware

steps.title: URL categories
steps.learn: URL categories apply the acceptable-use policy. **Warn** shows a page the user can click through, which is useful for gray areas.
steps.task: Block **Gambling** and **Malware Sites**, warn on **Social Networking**, and monitor **News**.
steps.screen: Secure Web Appliance › Access Policies › Global Policy › URL Filtering

summary: WCCP web-cache redirection of user HTTP traffic to the Secure Web Appliance, with WBRS block, scan and allow thresholds and URL category actions in the access policy.
